bull.t: Surf On Demand Growth And Margin Expansion
bull.b: Rapid growth in Surf On Demand revenue, departures, and revenue per departure indicates increasing customer adoption and route density. Concurrent gross-margin expansion suggests the model can improve economics as volume scales, supporting a more durable contribution to consolidated growth.

Positive airline adjusted EBITDA, improving each quarter in 2026, demonstrates progress toward a more sustainable operating model. Lower direct costs, fuel burn, and pilot costs per block hour can support recurring margin improvement if operating efficiency gains persist.

bull.t: SurfOS Commercial Launch And Strategic Traction
bull.b: SurfOS provides a technology-led growth avenue alongside the airline business, with commercial customer signings, FAA authorization, and enterprise discussions. Its transaction-based model and expanding pipeline could create higher-margin recurring revenue as implementations mature.

bear.t: Negative Equity And Reliance On External Capital
bear.b: Persistent negative equity leaves the company with a thin capital buffer and reduces flexibility during execution setbacks. The balance-sheet deficit, combined with reliance on external capital, can constrain investment choices and increase the importance of successful operating improvement.

Material operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that the core business is not yet self-funding. Continued cash consumption can require additional financing while SurfOS and airline initiatives scale, increasing funding dependence and limiting resilience if losses persist.

The scheduled-service decline reduces the contribution from an established revenue stream and reflects a smaller route footprint in affected markets. Although productivity improvements partly offset it, replacing that volume depends on continued growth in newer, less mature offerings.
